speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Ministry has new or additional plans to improve energy conservation and manage energy demand by businesses and households; and (b) if so, what are these plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Government also regularly reviews the support measures for businesses and households to become more energy efficient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In addition to support measures, the Government also regularly reviews the Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) and Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS) to continually shift the market towards more energy-efficient equipment and appliances.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will continue to consult closely with industry partners and the community to identify new technologies and ways to help businesses and households improve their energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I have this sense that the public and businesses may not all be familiar with these schemes.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, given the rising energy costs and our push to decarbonise, can I ask the Senior Minister of State if we should step up on public communications and to build this consciousness about energy conservation and to have visibility in some of these efforts as well, so as to get more buy-in?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My second question is whether, based on our current way of consumption, the Senior Minister of State sees further significant scope to conserve energy and whether it can really move the needle in terms of managing demand.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The various lead agencies – NEA, EDB, BCA, EMA and Enterprise Singapore – do reach out to the businesses through the trade associations and chambers, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: NEA also undertakes industry consultations as well as briefings to raise awareness among the industries and the businesses about the various schemes that we have to improve energy efficiency.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, we have been promoting and supporting energy conservation efforts, such as NEA's E2F fund.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, the Energy Efficiency Technology Centre, which is a collaboration between NEA and Singapore Institute of Technology, has been providing low-cost energy audits to some of the manufacturing SMEs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For Enterprise Singapore, too, they have their Enterprise Sustainability Programme (ESP) which they promote as well as the Resource Efficiency Grant for Energy in terms of emissions which EDB also promotes.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For households, as I have shared, we have the climate-friendly households programme for the 1-, 2- and 3-roomers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When we first started the programme, we sent out mailers to all the eligible households.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we are doing to encourage take-up is to work with the CDCs as well as with the community organisations on the ground to publicise this scheme and to do house-to-house visits.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are also sending SMSes to the eligible households who have not utilised the vouchers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we will continue to see how we can promote the scheme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As far as improving energy consumption is concerned, it is possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is also with the other schemes for the businesses.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I do have the numbers, but I think I can share that with the Member later.
